findings.quote: cross-field refinements mirroring the SQL checks (`youth_min_age <= youth_max_age`, `adult_min_age between youth_min_age and 21`
findings.problem: DESIGN §4.4 sketch defines `constraint youth_range check (youth_min_age >= 5 and youth_min_age < youth_max_age and youth_max_age <= 40)` (strict <, plus 5/40 bounds). The TS refinement accepts youth_min_age == youth_max_age and out-of-range values that the DB will reject with a 23514 the error map does not know. done_when repeats the looser rule ('rejects `youth_min_age > youth_max_age`').
findings.fix: Replace with: `youth_min_age >= 5`, `youth_min_age < youth_max_age`, `youth_max_age <= 40`, `adult_min_age >= youth_min_age && adult_min_age <= 21`, `directory_share_with_fellowship ⇒ directory_share_in_congregation` — copied from the `youth_range` / `adult_range` / `fellowship_implies_congregation` constraints in `9999_init.sql` section (3). Update done_when to 'rejects `youth_min_age >= youth_max_age`, `youth_min_age < 5`, `youth_max_age > 40`'. Also add `23514` → `invalid_payload` to the SQLSTATE fallback in Build 8.

findings.quote: `sermon`: `{ id, title, speaker, preached_on, description, media_kind, storage_path, external_url, mime_type }`, `org`: `{ name, logo_path }`
findings.problem: G2's 1.3b prompt (the migration this step mirrors) returns `sermon: {id, org_id, title, speaker, preached_on, description, media_kind, storage_path, external_url, external_id, mime_type}` and `org: {name, slug, logo_path}`. Dropping `external_id` (needed for the YouTube embed on /s/[token]) and `org_id`/`slug` silently strips them in a Zod object.
findings.fix: Change the `ok` payload to `sermon: { id, org_id, title, speaker, preached_on, description, media_kind, storage_path, external_url, external_id, mime_type }`, `org: { name, slug, logo_path }`, `allow_download` (still mirroring the migration if it differs).

findings.problem: 1.3b's `srv_resolve_share_link` returns only `{status}` for those outcomes; `sermon_title` / `org_name` are not in the migration or the docs. A required-field schema would reject the real response.
findings.fix: Model every non-`ok` status as `{ status }` with `link_id`, `sermon_title`, `org_name` OPTIONAL, and add an open_issue asking G2 (1.3b) to return `{status, link_id, sermon_title, org_name}` for `needs_password` / `needs_password_reset` so the password form can show a title; note the discrepancy in HANDOFF.

findings.fix: Write `acceptInvitationResultSchema` = `{ org_id, slug, membership_id, person_id }` (1.3b Build 6), 'or whatever the migration returns'.

findings.quote: `createInvitationSchema` field names follow the RPC parameters
findings.problem: open_issues says the invitation schema follows the RPC parameter names, but Build 9 defines `createInvitationSchema` (`org_id`, `email`, `person_id`, `permissions`) while the RPC parameters are `org`, `email`, `person_id`, `perms` (DESIGN §4.4 grant list / 1.3b). Same for `setMembershipPermissionsSchema.permissions` vs `perms`.
findings.fix: Either rename the schema fields to the RPC names (`org`, `perms`) or change the open_issue to say 'form schemas use `org_id`/`permissions`; the 1.7 wrappers translate to the SQL parameter names `org`/`perms`'.

findings.problem: `readMaxUploadMb(raw)` takes the env string; calling it without an argument always yields 50, so `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` (founder decision 10 lever for Pro) can never raise the cap. The package must not read `process.env` itself.
findings.fix: Make it a factory: `sermonUploadPlanSchema(maxUploadMb: number)` (web passes `readMaxUploadMb(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB)`), and cap additionally at `BUCKETS['sermon-media'].fileSizeLimitBytes`.

findings.problem: 1.2 fixed `calendars` with a `color text` column and `documents` with `description`; the schemas omit them although the prompt says the column names come from the migration.
findings.fix: Add `color` (nullable hex, reuse `hexColorSchema`) to `calendarSchema` and `description` (nullable) to `documentSchema`, keeping 'copy from the migration' as the rule.

findings.quote: `grep -c "public.srv_" supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` and the count of `srv*` exports in `src/rpc.ts` agree (7 functions)
